moodReason: The AI and chip selloff deepened on Wednesday after the S&P 500 had its worst week since April 2025. Inflation data showed the Fed's preferred gauge rising, which keeps rate-hike risk on the table going into a holiday-shortened week.

stories.headline: AI and chip selloff deepens as Nvidia drops and futures slide
stories.what: Nvidia fell about 6% on Tuesday after a sharp rally the session before, and chip stocks broadly dropped while the Nasdaq fell 1.48%. US index futures slid again on Wednesday as the AI chip selloff deepened.
stories.why: Nvidia and the chip group carry a large share of index weight and of AI-driven earnings expectations, so a continued slide drags the Nasdaq and the broader S&P 500 lower.

stories.headline: Fed's preferred inflation gauge rises, keeping December hike talk alive
stories.what: Wednesday's PCE inflation report showed the Fed's preferred gauge rising, and stocks fell that day alongside AI stocks. Oxford Economics had forecast headline PCE at 3.8% year on year for October, up from 3.6% in September.
stories.why: A hotter inflation reading raises the odds that the Fed tightens again at its December 9 meeting, which lifts Treasury yields and pressures valuations. Sources disagree on the market-implied odds, ranging from about 59% to 85%, so the exact pricing is unclear.

stories.headline: Nvidia leadership change and muted earnings reaction weigh on AI sentiment
stories.what: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's president, CEO and board member effective November 11, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Nvidia beat estimates in its fiscal Q3 report on November 17, but the shares barely reacted.
stories.why: Leadership uncertainty at the largest AI chip company, together with a weak reaction to a strong beat, has made investors more cautious about AI spending and valuations.

stories.headline: Sharp one-session rebound follows the S&P 500's worst week since April 2025
stories.what: On Monday the Dow rose about 1,448 points to 49,595.31, the S&P 500 gained 326.78 points to 7,237.17 and the Nasdaq Composite jumped about 1,472 points. The rebound came after the S&P 500 had its weakest week since April 2025 and finished the prior Friday more than 10% below its October record.
stories.why: The size of the bounce shows how volatile the market is right now. Traders are reading it as a relief move rather than a trend change, and the follow-through selling since then suggests the rebound has not held.

stories.headline: Traders weigh GDP revision and jobless claims in a short holiday week
stories.what: This week brings the third-quarter GDP revision and weekly jobless claims ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. Earnings from Best Buy and Workday came out Tuesday, and Dell's raised forecast did not stop its shares from falling.
stories.why: A revised growth figure and jobless data can shift expectations for the Fed's next move, which matters more while inflation is running hot.

Fed rate decision (hike odds are the key question)

bottomLine: Stocks are in a fragile, high-volatility stretch after the S&P 500's worst week since April 2025. The AI and chip group is the main source of stress, and Wednesday's firmer inflation reading keeps the Fed's next move in question. Traders head into a shortened holiday week with little room for more bad news from AI names or inflation.
